title: Two-block splicing of finite alternating ordinal strings
statement:
Use standard simplices and their monotone-map coordinates from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The inclusions of the two blocks of vertices $\Delta^m\to\Delta^{m+n}$ and $\Delta^n\to\Delta^{m+n}$ are induced by $i\mapsto i$ and $i\mapsto m+i$, respectively. The following gives the bijection on alternating strings for these two inclusions. For $r\geq0$ and $p,q\in\{-,+\}$, let $W_r(p,q)$ be the set of nonempty finite strings $(a_0,\ldots,a_w)$ in $\{0,1,\ldots,r+1\}$ with $a_0=p_r$, $a_w=q_r$, where $-_r=0$ and $+_r=r+1$. If $p=-$, require $a_i<a_{i+1}$ for even $i$ and $a_i>a_{i+1}$ for odd $i$; reverse these inequalities if $p=+$. Singleton strings are allowed. For any finite integer string $b$, define $R(b)$ by repeatedly deleting the leftmost adjacent equal pair until no adjacent equal letters remain. This is a deterministic finite algorithm and its value may be the empty string.

For $m,n\geq1$, define maps on integer alphabets
$$L(j)=\min(j,m+1),\quad U(j)=\max(j-m,0)\qquad(0\leq j\leq m+n+1).$$
On $\{0,\ldots,m+1\}$ put $v(j)=0$ for $j\leq m$ and $v(m+1)=1$. On $\{0,\ldots,n+1\}$ put $t(0)=0$ and $t(j)=1$ for $j>0$. Write $f_*a$ for entrywise application of an alphabet map $f$.

For each $p,q$, the assignment
$$c\longmapsto\big(R(L_*c),R(U_*c)\big)$$
is a bijection from $W_{m+n}(p,q)$ to
$$\{(a,b)\in W_m(p,q)\times W_n(p,q):R(v_*a)=R(t_*b)\}.$$
In particular both reduced block restrictions are nonempty and satisfy the indicated strict alternation. No bound on string length and no requirement to use all internal letters is imposed.

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Homotopy coherent adjunctions and the formal theory of monads, Proposition 3.2.2 and its proof, pp. 824--825; Definitions 3.1.2 and 3.1.8. The block restriction maps are the interval representations of {0,...,m} and {m,...,m+n}. Online paper read; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this finite-string splicing lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-adjunction-block-run-collapse] with r=m+n and h=m. It proves that every left/right block run of c has odd length, that C_m=L collapses each right run to one m+1, and that D_m=U collapses each left run to one 0, with no cross-run cancellation. The surviving runs retain their strict alternating inequalities and their endpoint values, so R(L_*c) lies in W_m(p,q) and R(U_*c) lies in W_n(p,q).

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Proposition 3.2.2 proof, pp. 824--825; Definitions 3.1.2 and 3.1.8. Online paper read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let d(c) be the word of 0's and 1's obtained by recording the labels of the maximal runs in c. Apply [lem-coef-adjunction-block-run-collapse] to the same cut in c. The preceding run calculation gives R(v_*R(L_*c))=d(c)=R(t_*R(U_*c)): on a 0-run the first expression records the unchanged left-block letters and the second records the single surviving 0, while on a 1-run they record the single m+1 and the unchanged right-block letters, respectively. Since d(c) has alternating labels, it is already reduced. Thus every image pair satisfies R(v_*a)=R(t_*b), and the compatibility word is exactly d(c).

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Proposition 3.2.2 proof, pp. 824--825; Definitions 3.1.2 and 3.1.8. Online paper read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Conversely, take (a,b) in the displayed compatible set and write d=R(v_*a)=R(t_*b). Apply [lem-coef-adjunction-block-run-collapse] to a with h=m and to b with h=0; this gives the same parity argument for the binary words v_*a and t_*b. Their maximal constant runs all have odd length and reduce to one letter, so d indexes corresponding runs A_k of a and B_k of b with the same label d_k. A 0-run B_k is a singleton, because t(b_i)=0 means b_i=0 and b is strictly alternating; a 1-run A_k is a singleton for the analogous reason v(a_i)=1 means a_i=m+1. Define c by concatenating A_k when d_k=0 and the entrywise shifted run m+B_k when d_k=1, in increasing k. The shifted runs lie in the right block. Each chosen run has odd length, and consecutive labels alternate; within runs the inequalities are inherited, while at a 0-to-1 join every left value is at most m and every right value is at least m+1, and at a 1-to-0 join the reverse inequality holds. The odd run lengths preserve the required parity of the alternating inequalities. The first and last labels give p and q, so c belongs to W_{m+n}(p,q).

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Proposition 3.2.2 proof, pp. 824--825; Definitions 3.1.2 and 3.1.8. Online paper read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-adjunction-block-run-collapse], for the c just constructed, L maps every chosen 0-run A_k identically and maps every shifted 1-run m+B_k to the constant value m+1. Each latter run has odd length, so reduction leaves one m+1; by the singleton property of the 1-runs A_k, the resulting word is exactly a. Dually, U maps each shifted 1-run m+B_k to B_k and each 0-run A_k to a constant 0-run of odd length, whose reduction is the singleton 0-run B_k. Hence R(L_*c)=a and R(U_*c)=b, proving surjectivity onto the compatible pairs.

source.place: Riehl--Verity, Proposition 3.2.2 proof, pp. 824--825; Definitions 3.1.2 and 3.1.8. Online paper read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: If c' has the same two reduced restrictions a and b, [lem-coef-adjunction-block-run-collapse] recovers its separator word d from either restriction. For each d_k=0, the corresponding c'-run is visible unchanged in R(L_*c') and therefore equals A_k; for d_k=1, it is visible unchanged after shifting in R(U_*c') and therefore equals m+B_k. Thus every run of c' agrees with the construction, so c'=c. This proves injectivity and the bijection. The argument also covers singleton words and words with no internal letters: then d has one run (or the corresponding alternating sequence of endpoint runs), and the same odd-run reduction and interleaving formulas apply without any extra length assumption.

lean.statement: theorem two_block_splicing (m n : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (p q : Bool) : Set.BijOn (fun c : List ℕ ↦ (reduce (c.map (lowerRestriction m)), reduce (c.map (upperRestriction m)))) {c : List ℕ | IsWord (m + n) p q c} {ab : List ℕ × List ℕ | IsWord m p q ab.1 ∧ IsWord n p q ab.2 ∧ reduce (ab.1.map (fun j : ℕ ↦ if j ≤ m then 0 else 1)) = reduce (ab.2.map (fun j : ℕ ↦ if j = 0 then 0 else 1))}
lean.note: Uses the already published AdjunctionWord definitions of the proof dependency, now added to stmt_deps. Set.BijOn expresses the stated map into exactly the compatible pairs, including nonemptiness and strict alternation of both restrictions.
